title: AutoAMM
tagline: An autonomous research lab that tests and refines programmable market-making strategies.
description: AutoAMM brings the autoresearch loop to market making: propose a strategy change, run an experiment, evaluate it against the incumbent, and keep or reject the result. The prototype searches fee levels and active capital allocations for a WETH/USDC constant-product strategy. Candidates must pass drawdown and inventory limits and improve on both training and validation scenarios. A separate holdout is unlocked at the end of a 24-experiment run. The Next.js dashboard exposes the experiment journal, rejection reasons, performance comparisons, strategy code, and downloadable evidence. Accepted parameters compile into real 1inch Aqua/SwapVM program bytecode and unsigned transaction plans. The public demo uses a deterministic heuristic optimizer and synthetic order flow; it does not sign transactions or claim simulated results are live trading profits. A server-side Graph adapter supports indexed market prices when credentials are configured.
how_its_made: Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Recharts, Zod, viem, and the official 1inch Aqua and SwapVM SDKs. The deterministic constant-product simulator models fee-sensitive order flow, arbitrage, retained fees, and estimated execution costs. An autonomous search loop explores fee levels and capital allocations while a fixed evaluator checks net equity relative to HODL on training and validation paths. The dashboard streams the resulting experiment history and unlocks a separate holdout after 24 candidates. The Aqua compiler combines flatFeeAmountInXD with xycSwapXD and prepares token approvals and ship calldata using the official SDKs. A server-side Graph adapter queries and validates hourly WETH/USDC pool prices. The Vercel deployment intentionally contains no market-data, model, or wallet keys. Simulation and bytecode compilation work without credentials; live-data access and transaction signing are separate. Drawdown and inventory-percentage gates are offchain evaluator checks, not guarantees encoded in the compiled program. Codex provided substantial coding and design assistance.
auto_summary: A Next.js app simulates and evaluates market-making strategies, then compiles selected parameters into 1inch Aqua/SwapVM transaction plans.
